questions.question:
Issue 1 (Pass 1, gap G1) — How should the header action group signal that Save is the primary action?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md Settings Page UI redesign, action row Save | Reset | Cancel | Export.
ELI10: Right now all four header buttons look identical, so a user scanning the page has to read every label to find Save. DESIGN.md already says Save is the only filled primary button (#1d4ed8 fill, white text) and Reset/Cancel/Export are neutral ghost buttons. This decides whether the plan adopts that token so the eye lands on Save first.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users hunt for Save on every visit, and the action nearest the fields (Export, at the row's end) gets mis-clicked; the plan's own gap list flags exactly this.
Recommendation: 1A because DESIGN.md prescribes it, the Button component already has the primary/ghost variants, and it maps to the principle "every screen has a hierarchy; if everything competes, nothing wins."
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=6/10, 1C=3/10
Pros / cons:
1A) Save filled primary #1d4ed8/white; Reset, Cancel, Export neutral ghost (recommended)
  ✅ One accent in the header; the eye lands on Save in the 3-second scan without reading labels
  ✅ Reuses the existing Button variants and DESIGN.md tokens; no new component or color (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
  ❌ Three ghost buttons still sit at equal weight with each other; destructive intent stays in the dialog, not the button
B) Save primary plus a visual divider or extra gap isolating Export from Reset/Cancel
  ✅ Also separates the download action from the two discard actions
  ✅ Still one accent color in the header
  ❌ Adds a layout decision DESIGN.md never approved, and the equal-column row at ≤640px has no room for a divider
C) Keep four equal buttons, rely on Save being first in order
  ✅ Zero change to the current implementation
  ✅ DOM order already puts Save first
  ❌ Order alone fails the scan test and contradicts DESIGN.md's single filled primary; the gap stays open
Net: adopt the approved primary/ghost split now, or keep an ambiguous header that contradicts the design system.

options.label: 1A Save primary, others ghost (recommended)
options.description:
✅ One accent, Save found at a glance
✅ Existing Button variants and tokens
❌ Ghost trio still equal to each other

options.label: 1B Primary plus divider before Export
options.description:
✅ Separates download from discard actions
✅ Still one accent
❌ Unapproved layout; no room at 640px

options.label: 1C Keep four equal buttons
options.description:
✅ No change
✅ Save already first in DOM
❌ Fails scan test, contradicts DESIGN.md

questions.question:
Issue 2 (Pass 2, gap G5) — What does the user see during the 2–5 second Save request?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md Settings Page UI redesign, Save button pending state.
ELI10: Today the page freezes for up to five seconds after clicking Save, so people click again or assume it failed. The plan already says pending feedback lives in the button (not the status text) and already gives Export an inline spinner beside "Exporting…". DESIGN.md defines the same pattern for Save: spinner beside "Saving…" inside the button, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion support. The plan's gap note says "spinner or skeleton"; this decides which.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a skeleton would hide the very fields the plan promises to preserve on failure, and a silent 5-second wait keeps depleting trust on every save.
Recommendation: 2A because it is the established pattern, mirrors Export exactly, keeps the user's edits visible, and honors "do not repeat Saving… in the status live region." Principle: trust is earned at the pixel level; the user must see their action was received.
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=4/10, 2C=5/10
Pros / cons:
2A) Inline spinner beside "Saving…" inside the aria-disabled Save button, aria-busy=true, reduced motion honored (recommended)
  ✅ Same component and motion as Export, so one pattern to build and test (human: ~2h / CC: ~10min)
  ✅ Fields stay visible and editable-looking, matching the promise that edits survive a failure
  ❌ On a 2-second save the spinner is brief; the timestamp in the status is what confirms success, not the spinner
B) Replace the form with the loading skeleton during Save
  ✅ Very obvious that something is happening
  ✅ Reuses the existing load skeleton
  ❌ Hides the user's edits mid-save and forces a layout swap; on failure the form must re-mount, and focus rules (no focus move while pending) get hard to keep
C) Spinner in the button plus "Saving…" in the InlineStatus live region
  ✅ Screen-reader users hear the pending state without focusing the button
  ✅ Still keeps fields visible
  ❌ Directly contradicts DESIGN.md ("do not repeat Saving… in the status live region") and would announce twice on every save
Net: adopt the button-scoped spinner the design system already defines, or diverge from Export's established pattern.

options.label: 2A Spinner + "Saving…" in Save button (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Mirrors Export exactly
✅ Edits stay visible
❌ Brief on fast saves; timestamp confirms

options.label: 2B Skeleton during Save
options.description:
✅ Unmistakable pending state
✅ Reuses load skeleton
❌ Hides edits, breaks focus rules

options.label: 2C Spinner + status text "Saving…"
options.description:
✅ Announced without focus
✅ Fields visible
❌ Contradicts DESIGN.md, double announce

questions.question:
Issue 3 (Pass 5, gap G2) — Which vertical rhythm should the form use between sections and fields?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md Settings Page UI redesign, spacing between action group, Profile and Notifications.
ELI10: The current form mixes 16px, 24px and 32px gaps with no rule, so the eye can't tell where one group ends and the next starts. DESIGN.md defines an 8px base scale: 32px between sections, 24px between field groups, 8px from label to input. This decides whether the plan adopts that scale everywhere on the page.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the Gestalt proximity cue breaks; fields look loosely related to their heading, and the header actions can read as part of the Profile section.
Recommendation: 3A because it is the approved scale, it needs no new tokens, and it maps to "related things are visually grouped; nested things are visually contained."
Completeness: 3A=10/10, 3B=6/10, 3C=2/10
Pros / cons:
3A) Adopt DESIGN.md scale: sections 32px, field groups 24px, label-to-input 8px, everywhere including header→status→Profile (recommended)
  ✅ One rule the implementer can apply without judgment calls; every gap is a multiple of 8 (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
  ✅ Section gap (32) is clearly larger than field gap (24), so grouping reads at a glance
  ❌ Slightly taller page than the tightest current 16px gaps; on 320px screens one more scroll line
B) Normalize only the section gaps to 32px, leave field gaps as they are
  ✅ Smallest visual change
  ✅ Fixes the most visible inconsistency
  ❌ Leaves 16px and 24px field gaps unresolved, so the rhythm inside sections stays uneven
C) Keep current mixed spacing
  ✅ No work
  ✅ No risk of unexpected layout shifts
  ❌ The plan's own gap stays open and the form still contradicts DESIGN.md
Net: one 8px rule for the whole page vs. a partial or no fix.

options.label: 3A Adopt 32/24/8 scale everywhere (recommended)
options.description:
✅ One rule, no judgment calls
✅ Grouping reads at a glance
❌ Slightly taller page

options.description:
✅ Smallest change

❌ Gap stays open

questions.question:
Issue 4 (Pass 5, gap G3) — Which error colors should the form use?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md Settings Page UI redesign, field errors, ErrorSummary and network-error rows.
ELI10: The current error text is red on light pink at roughly 3:1 contrast, below the 4.5:1 WCAG AA minimum for body text. That is the message people read under stress ("Couldn't save your changes"). DESIGN.md already defines error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2, which measures about 7.5:1, plus an icon and explicit wording so status never relies on color alone. This decides whether the plan adopts those tokens.
Stakes if we pick wrong: users with low vision or on a dim screen can't read why the save failed, and the form fails an accessibility audit.
Recommendation: 4A because the approved tokens clear AA with margin, they already carry the icon-plus-text rule, and this maps to "accessibility is not optional."
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=7/10, 4C=1/10
Pros / cons:
4A) error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2 with the existing icon and explicit text, for field errors, ErrorSummary and network-error rows (recommended)
  ✅ ~7.5:1 contrast, clears AA for body text and AAA for the 16px size (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
  ✅ Icon plus wording means colorblind users still get the state; matches every existing error surface
  ❌ Darker red reads less "alarm-red" than the current tone; that is intentional but a visual change
B) Keep current red text, darken it until it measures at least 4.5:1 on the pink
  ✅ Minimal token churn
  ✅ Meets AA once measured
  ❌ Invents a third red outside DESIGN.md and needs measuring per surface; the pink surface itself stays unspecified
C) Keep the current ~3:1 pair
  ✅ No work
  ✅ Familiar to current users
  ❌ Fails WCAG AA; the plan's own gap stays open
Net: adopt the approved error pair now or keep an audit failure in the most stressful moment of the journey.

options.label: 4A #991b1b on #fef2f2 + icon + text (recommended)
options.description:
✅ ~7.5:1 contrast
✅ Icon + text, not color alone
❌ Visibly different red

options.label: 4B Darken current red to 4.5:1
options.description:
✅ Minimal churn
✅ Meets AA
❌ Third red outside DESIGN.md

questions.question:
Issue 5 (Pass 5, gap G4) — Which type scale should form labels, helper text and section headings use?
Project/branch/task: main branch, PLAN.md Settings Page UI redesign, Profile and Notifications labels and headings.
ELI10: Labels currently come in 14px, 16px and 18px with no rule, so some labels look more important than others for no reason and the 14px ones are below the 16px body minimum. DESIGN.md defines two roles: 16px for body, form labels and helper text; 20px for section headings. This decides whether the plan adopts that two-role scale.
Stakes if we pick wrong: the h2 headings don't visibly outrank an 18px label, and 14px helper text is hard to read on phones.
Recommendation: 5A because two roles is exactly the hierarchy the plan's gap note asks for, it lifts every label to the 16px floor, and it maps to "omit, then omit again": one distinction, heading vs. everything else.
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=6/10, 5C=2/10
Pros / cons:
5A) Adopt DESIGN.md: 16px labels/helper/body, 20px h2 section headings, nothing else (recommended)
  ✅ Headings are the only larger text, so the two sections are found by size alone (human: ~1h / CC: ~5min)
  ✅ No text on the page below 16px; helper and error text become readable on 320px screens
  ❌ Labels that were 18px shrink slightly; anyone used to the current form will notice
B) Two sizes but keep 14px for helper text as a third role
  ✅ Tighter helper text under inputs
  ✅ Labels still unified at 16px
  ❌ Adds a role DESIGN.md doesn't have and drops helper text below the 16px body floor
C) Keep 14/16/18 as is
  ✅ No work
  ✅ Nothing moves
  ❌ Three sizes with no rule; the plan's own gap stays open
Net: the approved two-role scale vs. a third size or no fix.

Noted: routing rules approved. Plan mode blocks the CLAUDE.md edit and commit right now, so I'll do it after plan mode ends. Continuing with the pre-review audit.

**Pass 1 re-rate: 6/10 → 10/10.** The header now has one primary, the reading order is Save → status → secondary actions, and the ASCII structure plus arrival/exit flows were already in the plan. No further IA issues.

## Pass 2: Interaction State Coverage — 7/10

State table as the plan currently specifies it (what the user sees):

```
FEATURE          | LOADING                          | EMPTY                              | ERROR                                        | SUCCESS                        | PARTIAL
-----------------|----------------------------------|------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------------
Page load        | existing form skeleton           | new account: DESIGN.md defaults    | "Couldn't load your settings." + Retry       | populated form, blank status   | n/a (atomic read)
Save             | ❌ UNSPECIFIED (2–5s frozen)      | clean Save is a no-op              | "Couldn't save your changes. Your edits are  | "Saved at HH:mm" in status     | never exposed (atomic)
                 |                                  |                                    | still here." + Retry (aria-label Retry save) |                                |
Export           | "Exporting…" + spinner in button | n/a (exports saved prefs)          | "Couldn't prepare your export." + Retry      | file download, error cleared   | n/a
Reset            | HTML disabled while pending      | disabled when clean                | n/a                                          | dialog → values + status back  | n/a
Cancel           | HTML disabled while pending      | clean: navigates immediately       | n/a                                          | dialog → leave                 | n/a
Field validation | n/a                              | n/a                                | inline + ErrorSummary, focus first invalid   | errors clear                   | n/a
InlineStatus     | text unchanged while pending     | blank before first save            | "Unsaved changes" persists beside error      | "Saved at HH:mm"               | n/a
```

One hole: the Save loading state (G5). The plan says "Pending feedback belongs to the request button" and specifies that pattern for Export, but for Save it only says "add a spinner or skeleton state". Everything else is covered.

**Pass 2 re-rate: 7/10 → 10/10.** Every row of the state table now has a visible answer; the Save loading hole is closed with the existing pattern.

## Pass 3: User Journey & Emotional Arc — 9/10

Storyboard of the accepted journey (recorded, not a new decision):

```
STEP | USER DOES                        | USER FEELS                          | PLAN SPECIFIES?
-----|----------------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------
1    | Arrives from account nav         | Oriented: "this is my settings"     | h1 "Account settings" + verbatim description; skeleton, not blank, while loading
2    | Scans for what to change         | Calm; two clear groups              | Profile / Notifications h2 fieldsets, labels visible, defaults pre-filled for new accounts
3    | Edits a field                    | Aware something is now different    | Status flips to "Unsaved changes" (text, not color)
4    | Looks for Save                   | Certain which button                | D-1: single filled primary
5    | Clicks Save, waits 2–5s          | Reassured it was received           | D-2: spinner + "Saving…", repeat clicks guarded
6a   | Save succeeds                    | Done; trusts it stuck               | "Saved at HH:mm", no focus jump, Export now reflects saved prefs
6b   | Save fails                       | Annoyed but not panicked            | "Couldn't save your changes. Your edits are still here." + Retry; edits preserved; focus only moves if still on Save
7    | Leaves (Cancel / nav / tab close)| Safe from losing work               | Clean: leave immediately; dirty: dialog, default "Keep editing"; beforeunload only while dirty
```

Time horizons: 5-second visceral is served by the title, description and (after D-1) one obvious primary. 5-minute behavioral is served by the status text and error recovery. 5-year reflective: the timestamp and atomic save build the habit of trusting this page. The one place the arc still dips is step 6b at the pixel level: the error message the user reads under stress is the one with ~3:1 contrast (G3). That is a color/design-system defect and is asked in Pass 5; it is what keeps this pass at 9 until resolved. No new journey-specific remedy to propose, so no question here.

## Pass 4: AI Slop Risk — 10/10

**Classifier: OPERATE (app UI, settings form).** Scanability and native expectations beat expression.

Hard rejections: none. No card grid, no hero, no stacked-card layout; the form is a single column of fieldsets.

Litmus: (1) Brand unmistakable: YES, persistent app navigation + h1 inside the product shell. (2) One visual anchor: YES after D-1 (Save primary). (3) Scannable by headings: YES, h1 → Profile → Notifications. (4) One job per section: YES. (5) Cards necessary: N/A, none used. (6) Motion improves hierarchy: YES, the only motion is the pending spinner, which carries state. (7) Premium without shadows: YES, none specified.

App UI rules: calm surface, one accent (#1d4ed8), utility copy ("Saved at HH:mm", "Unsaved changes"), headings name the area. Universal rules: 16px minimum body, visible labels (not placeholder-as-label), CSS-variable-worthy tokens named by hex. The `system-ui, sans-serif` stack is on the blacklist as a display voice, but here it is an explicitly retained existing constraint (PLAN.md and DESIGN.md line 29) on an Operate surface where the rules allow an assigned UI font; recorded under NOT in scope, not a finding. No issues, moving on.

## Pass 5: Design System Alignment — 4/10

DESIGN.md exists and the plan body is faithful to its behavior. The three remaining listed deltas are all token violations: spacing (G2), error color (G3), label type scale (G4). Each is a separate token family, so each gets its own decision.

questions.question:
D3 — Issue 1: How should Save be distinguished from Reset/Cancel/Export in the header?
Project/branch/task: main, Settings Page UI redesign plan, Pass 1 (Information Architecture).
ELI10: The header has four buttons that look identical. Users scan, they don't read, so the first thing they should register is the one action that finishes their task: Save. When Save looks like Cancel, people hesitate or mis-click a destructive-adjacent button. DESIGN.md already says Save is the only filled button.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Either the primary action stays invisible in the row (hesitation, mis-clicks on Cancel/Reset), or we invent a second visual language that drifts from the design system.
Recommendation: 1A because it is the exact DESIGN.md token, changes no geometry or order, and gives the row one obvious anchor (Design Principle 2: every screen has a hierarchy).
Completeness: 1A=10/10, 1B=6/10, 1C=3/10
Pros / cons:
1A) Adopt DESIGN.md: Save filled #1d4ed8 with white text; Reset, Cancel, Export neutral ghost buttons (recommended)
  ✅ One visual anchor in the row, matching the approved system with zero new tokens
  ✅ Same 44px geometry and DOM order, so the ≤640px layout and tab order are untouched
  ❌ Disabled and pending appearances of the filled button must be checked against the existing Button styles
1B) Filled Save plus a visual separator or extra gap isolating Export from Reset/Cancel
  ✅ Also separates the non-destructive Export from the two discard actions
  ✅ Still keeps Save as the single filled control in the row
  ❌ Adds an unapproved layout token and a stacked-row edge case at 640px that DESIGN.md does not define
1C) Keep four identical buttons; rely on Save being first in order
  ✅ Zero implementation work in this change
  ✅ No risk of touching Button styles
  ❌ Leaves the documented DESIGN.md violation and the hesitation problem in place
Net: adopting the approved token gets a 10 here for free; anything else trades system consistency for speculative gains.

options.label: 1A) Filled Save, ghost secondaries per DESIGN.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ One visual anchor, exact approved tokens, no new vocabulary
✅ Geometry, DOM and tab order unchanged at every width
❌ Must verify existing Button disabled/pending styles on the filled variant

options.label: 1B) Filled Save plus separator isolating Export
options.description:
✅ Also distances Export from the two discard actions
✅ Save still the only filled control
❌ Unapproved layout token; undefined behavior in the 640px stacked row

options.label: 1C) Keep four identical buttons
options.description:

✅ Button styles untouched
❌ DESIGN.md violation and hesitation problem remain

answers.D3 — Issue 1: How should Save be disting: 1A) Filled Save, ghost secondaries per DESIGN.md (recommended)

questions.question:
D4 — Issue 2: What does the user see during the 2-5 second Save?
Project/branch/task: main, Settings Page UI redesign plan, Pass 2 (Interaction State Coverage).
ELI10: When someone clicks Save, nothing changes for up to five seconds. People assume the click didn't register and click again or leave. The plan already blocks repeat submissions, but blocking without feedback just makes the button feel broken. DESIGN.md's established pattern is a small spinner beside the word "Saving…" inside the Save button, with aria-busy so screen readers know, and no spinner for users who turned motion off.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A frozen-looking page erodes the trust the whole journey is built on ("were my preferences stored?"); a page-level skeleton would hide the very fields the user just edited and contradicts the accepted rule that pending feedback lives on the request button.
Recommendation: 2A because it is the accepted DESIGN.md pattern, keeps edits visible, and mirrors what the plan already specifies for Export (Nielsen: visibility of system status).
Completeness: 2A=10/10, 2B=5/10, 2C=2/10
Pros / cons:
2A) DESIGN.md pattern: inline spinner beside “Saving…” inside the aria-disabled Save button, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion shows text only; InlineStatus text unchanged; no focus move (recommended)
  ✅ Feedback exactly where the user is looking, edits stay visible, matches the Export treatment already in the plan
  ✅ Screen readers get aria-busy on the trigger without a second live-region announcement
  ❌ Button width can shift when “Save” becomes “Saving…”; the button must reserve width or tolerate the change
2B) Form-level skeleton or overlay while saving
  ✅ Very obvious that something is happening
  ✅ Reuses the existing load skeleton
  ❌ Hides the fields the user just edited and contradicts the accepted rule that pending feedback belongs to the request button
2C) Keep it as is: disabled Save, no indicator
  ✅ No implementation work
  ✅ No motion to make reduced-motion safe
  ❌ Users see a frozen page for 2-5 seconds, the exact complaint the plan records
Net: the button-local spinner is the approved, lowest-risk way to say "working on it"; the alternatives are either heavier or leave the page looking broken.

options.label: 2A) Spinner + “Saving…” in the Save button per DESIGN.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Feedback where the user looks; edits stay visible; matches Export
✅ aria-busy on the trigger, no duplicate live announcement
❌ Must handle width change from “Save” to “Saving…”

options.label: 2B) Form-level skeleton/overlay while saving
options.description:
✅ Unmistakable activity signal
✅ Reuses the load skeleton
❌ Hides edited fields; contradicts accepted button-local pending rule

options.label: 2C) Keep disabled Save with no indicator
options.description:
✅ No work
✅ No motion concerns
❌ Frozen-looking page for 2-5 seconds remains

answers.D4 — Issue 2: What does the user see dur: 2A) Spinner + “Saving…” in the Save button per DESIGN.md (recommended)

questions.question:
D5 — Issue 3: Which type sizes should the form's labels and headings use?
Project/branch/task: main, Settings Page UI redesign plan, Pass 4 (AI Slop Risk, universal type rules).
ELI10: The form labels are currently a mix of 14px, 16px and 18px. Three sizes for one kind of text reads as accidental, and 14px is below the 16px floor for body text (harder to read, especially on phones). DESIGN.md defines just two roles: 16px for body, labels and helper text, and 20px for the Profile/Notifications headings. Fewer sizes, used consistently, create a stronger hierarchy than more sizes.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Keep three sizes and labels stay inconsistent with 14px text under the readability floor; invent a third role and we drift from the system for no user benefit.
Recommendation: 3A because it is the approved token set, removes the sub-16px text, and the h1 stays whatever the existing shell renders (this plan does not touch it), so nothing new is invented (Design Principle 3: specificity over vibes).
Completeness: 3A=10/10, 3B=6/10, 3C=3/10
Pros / cons:
3A) DESIGN.md two roles: 16px for all labels, helper, body, button and status text; 20px for the h2 section headings; h1 keeps its existing shell style (recommended)
  ✅ Exactly two roles, every label identical, no text below 16px anywhere on the form
  ✅ Section headings read as headings; h1 untouched so the page title stays consistent with other app pages
  ❌ Existing 14px helper or status text grows, so 320px layouts must be re-checked for wrapping
3B) Two roles but keep 14px for helper/status text as a third "small" role
  ✅ Slightly denser status and helper rows
  ✅ Labels themselves become consistent at 16px
  ❌ Adds an unapproved 14px role below the readability floor; DESIGN.md says helper text is 16px
3C) Keep the current 14/16/18px mix
  ✅ No work in this change
  ✅ No re-check of 320px wrapping
  ❌ Inconsistent labels stay, 14px text stays, the documented gap stays open
Net: two roles is the whole point; the only reason to add a third is density, and this form has five fields, so density is not the constraint.

options.label: 3A) 16px labels/body, 20px h2, h1 unchanged per DESIGN.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Two roles, all labels identical, nothing under 16px
✅ h1 untouched, consistent with other app pages
❌ Grown helper/status text needs a 320px wrap re-check

options.label: 3B) 16px labels, 20px h2, keep 14px helper/status
options.description:
✅ Denser helper and status rows
✅ Labels consistent at 16px
❌ Unapproved 14px role below the readability floor

options.label: 3C) Keep the 14/16/18px mix
options.description:
✅ No work
✅ No wrap re-check
❌ Inconsistent labels and sub-16px text remain

answers.D5 — Issue 3: Which type sizes should th: 3A) 16px labels/body, 20px h2, h1 unchanged per DESIGN.md (recommended)

questions.question:
D6 — Issue 4: What vertical rhythm should the form use?
Project/branch/task: main, Settings Page UI redesign plan, Pass 5 (Design System Alignment).
ELI10: Right now the gaps between parts of the form are 16px in one place, 24px in another and 32px in a third, with no rule behind them. Users don't consciously notice spacing, but uneven gaps make a page feel sloppy and make it harder to tell where one group ends and the next begins. DESIGN.md gives an 8px scale: 32px between sections, 24px between field groups, 8px from a label to its input. The header (title, description, actions, status) has no named token, so the plan needs to say which scale steps it uses there too.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Leave it and the form keeps its uneven rhythm and the heading-proximity rule (more space above a heading than below it) stays unenforced; pick ad hoc numbers for the header and we create a second, undocumented scale.
Recommendation: 4A because it applies the approved tokens everywhere and maps the header onto the same three steps, so every gap on the page is 8, 24 or 32 (Gestalt proximity: spacing tells the user what belongs together).
Completeness: 4A=10/10, 4B=7/10, 4C=3/10
Pros / cons:
4A) DESIGN.md scale everywhere: 32px between sections (status area→Profile, Profile→Notifications), 24px between field groups, 8px label→input; header mapped onto the same steps: 8px h1→description, 24px description→action row, 24px action row→status slot; h2 sits 32px below the previous block and 24px above its first field (recommended)
  ✅ Every gap on the page is one of three approved values, including the header rows
  ✅ Headings are closer to what follows (24px) than to what precedes (32px), satisfying the proximity rule
  ❌ Header mapping is a plan-level interpretation of the 8px base, so it should be recorded back into DESIGN.md later
4B) Apply DESIGN.md tokens to the sections and fields only; leave header spacing as currently built
  ✅ Smaller change, touches only the fieldset styles
  ✅ Section rhythm becomes consistent
  ❌ Header stays on unnamed values, so the top of the page keeps its own rhythm
4C) Keep the current 16/24/32px mix
  ✅ No work
  ✅ No layout re-check needed
  ❌ The documented inconsistency stays; heading proximity is not guaranteed
Net: the scale exists; the only real choice is whether the header joins it or stays a special case.

options.label: 4A) 8/24/32 scale everywhere, header mapped onto it (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Every gap is 8, 24 or 32px, header included
✅ Headings closer to what follows than what precedes
❌ Header mapping should be written back to DESIGN.md later

options.label: 4B) Tokens on sections/fields only, header unchanged
options.description:
✅ Smaller change, fieldset styles only
✅ Section rhythm consistent
❌ Header keeps unnamed spacing values

options.label: 4C) Keep the current 16/24/32px mix
options.description:
✅ No work
✅ No layout re-check
❌ Inconsistency and unenforced heading proximity remain

answers.D6 — Issue 4: What vertical rhythm shoul: 4A) 8/24/32 scale everywhere, header mapped onto it (recommended)

questions.question:
D7 — Issue 5: Which colors should the error message use?
Project/branch/task: main, Settings Page UI redesign plan, Pass 5 (Design System Alignment) and Pass 6 (Accessibility).
ELI10: The error message is red text on light pink at roughly 3:1 contrast. WCAG AA needs 4.5:1 for text, so people with low vision or a dim phone screen can miss the one message that tells them their save failed. DESIGN.md already specifies error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2, which I computed at about 7.7:1 (passes AA and AAA), with an icon and explicit text so the state never depends on color alone.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Users who most need the message (failed save, edits at risk) are the least able to read it, and the plan keeps a documented accessibility failure.
Recommendation: 5A because it is the approved token pair, passes AA with margin, and keeps the icon + text redundancy already in the plan (Design Principle 7: accessibility is not optional).
Completeness: 5A=10/10, 5B=7/10, 5C=2/10
Pros / cons:
5A) DESIGN.md pair: #991b1b text on #fef2f2 surface, existing error icon, explicit text; applies to the Save, Export and Load error rows and to inline field errors on their existing surface (recommended)
  ✅ About 7.7:1 contrast, comfortably past AA 4.5:1, using tokens the system already names
  ✅ Same pair for every error surface on the page, so failure always looks the same
  ❌ Ghost Retry button and error icon must also be re-checked at 3:1 against the #fef2f2 surface
5B) Keep the current red, drop the pink background so the red sits on white
  ✅ Likely passes AA depending on the exact red
  ✅ Minimal change to the existing styles
  ❌ Diverges from DESIGN.md's named surface and loses the visual grouping of the error row
5C) Keep red on pink as is
  ✅ No work
  ✅ No re-check of icon and Retry contrast
  ❌ The AA failure stays on the most important message in the flow
Net: the approved pair fixes the contrast and unifies every error surface; the alternatives either drift or leave the failure in place.

options.label: 5A) #991b1b on #fef2f2 with icon + text per DESIGN.md (recommended)
options.description:
✅ ~7.7:1 contrast, approved tokens
✅ One consistent look for every error surface
❌ Re-check ghost Retry and icon at 3:1 on #fef2f2

options.label: 5B) Current red on white, no pink surface
options.description:
✅ Probably passes AA
✅ Minimal style change
❌ Drifts from DESIGN.md; loses error-row grouping

options.label: 5C) Keep red on pink as is
options.description:
✅ No work
✅ No contrast re-check
❌ AA failure stays on the key failure message

answers.D7 — Issue 5: Which colors should the er: 5A) #991b1b on #fef2f2 with icon + text per DESIGN.md (recommended)
